description: Imports Facebook/Meta ad accounts, campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, activities, media assets and Ads Insights reports (with breakdowns) from the Facebook Graph Marketing API.

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment: API_VERSION = "v25.0" is interpolated into BASE_URL (and into both OAuth2 URL templates)

credentialModes.name: OAuth app + long-lived user access token

artifacts: Facebook-side async insights report jobs (report_run_id), one per submitted insights job; jobs are split recursively on failure so a single sweep can create many
continuity.ourSideLoss: Insights data older than 37 months becomes unqueryable (DATA_RETENTION_PERIOD = 37 months; start_date is clamped forward to the retention boundary). An in-flight async report job that is not polled within MAX_JOB_WAIT_TIME (1 hour) is abandoned and must be resubmitted.
continuity.resumeWindow: 37 months for insights backfill; 1 hour for an individual in-flight async report job
continuity.notes: Pure polling connector: no server-side subscription, slot, or consumer group. On shutdown the job manager only cancels local asyncio tasks (_cancel_pending); it never issues a delete/cancel to Facebook for submitted report_run_ids, so abandoned report jobs are left to expire on Facebook's side. Nothing accrues on the customer's infrastructure. Entity streams (campaigns/ads/etc.) are re-swept from the stored timestamp cursor, so an arbitrarily long pause is safe for them.

authTierRationale: Exactly one credential mode is offered. Standalone, the user must supply all three of client_id, client_secret and access_token (all required in the endpoint config schema) — i.e. register their own Meta app AND obtain a long-lived user access token with ads_management/ads_read/read_insights/business_management. That is strictly more work than T2_BYO_APP, so it is bucketed T3, with the caveat that the third artifact is a long-lived ACCESS token, not a refresh token: the CDK's TokenSource returns LongLivedClientCredentialsOAuth2Credentials.access_token verbatim as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and never performs a token exchange at runtime. Estuary's hosted control plane can collapse this to a click-through: the connector spec ships an oauth2 block (provider "facebook", authorization_code dialog + access_token exchange) and the credentials model is tagged x-oauth2-provider: facebook, so the control plane registers/holds the app and fills all three fields. The standalone tier is what is recorded here.

unionMisfits.description: Insights are not a single HTTP read. Each bounded slice is a three-call async job: POST /act_{account_id}/insights (returns report_run_id) -> repeated GET /{report_run_id} polling async_status/async_percent_completion every 30s up to 1h -> GET /{report_run_id}/insights to read pages. The PullSpec union has no way to express submit/poll/read, so only the final read leg is modelled in `path`/`paginator` and the first two legs are described in pathPlaceholders.

proposedShape.onOverload: recursive bisection: split the job by campaign -> adset -> ad, discovering child entity IDs via a synchronous insights query, until a single-ad job is atomic

unionMisfits.description: The incremental bound is not a scalar query parameter. It is a `filtering` query param carrying a JSON-encoded array of predicate objects {field, operator, value}, where field is "<entity_prefix>.<cursor_field>" and value is a Unix-seconds integer. The backfill leg sends TWO predicates (GREATER_THAN start_date AND LESS_THAN cutoff); the incremental leg sends one (GREATER_THAN log_cursor). When include_deleted is set, a third unrelated predicate (delivery_info IN [...]) is appended to the same param.

Insights bound their slice with a `time_range` param holding a JSON object {since, until} of YYYY-MM-DD dates, plus time_increment=1 for daily granularity. It is a closed interval, not a single since-value, so {param, format} loses the `until` side.

These two streams have NO server-side incremental filter at all. Facebook returns adimages/advideos in descending updated_time order, and the connector performs a full paginated sweep that breaks out of the loop as soon as a document with updated_time <= log_cursor is seen. Correctness depends entirely on the API's undeclared DESC ordering. Images additionally filters deleted records client-side because Facebook returns them regardless of the filter.

clientSideFilters: status == deleted (images only, when include_deleted is false)

unionMisfits.description: The tier ladder discriminates T2 from T3 on the presence of a REFRESH token. This connector requires a third secret that is a long-lived ACCESS token which is never exchanged or rotated. Burden matches T3; mechanism does not.

One binding fans out over N ad accounts from the comma-separated account_ids config. Incremental bindings keep a SEPARATE cursor and backfill state per account id (ResourceState.inc / .backfill are dicts keyed by account id, reconciled on open so newly added accounts get fresh state), and full-refresh bindings interleave per-account generators with a concurrency of len(accounts). The schema models a stream as having one cursor.

The `limit` query param is not a fixed page size. A should_retry hook inspects 5xx bodies for "reduce"/"too much data"/"retry"/"unknown error" and halves `limit` in place (floor 1) before retrying, up to 15 attempts. The declared pageSize of 25 is only the starting value.

The requested field list is not static. Before each request a PermissionManager queries /me/business_users and /act_{id}/assigned_users to compute the caller's tasks and drops fields the account lacks permission for; on top of that, a permission error at request time is caught, the offending field is regex-identified from the error message, removed, and the request retried. So the emitted document shape varies by grantee permissions.

abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No static headers are set anywhere in the connector; the only header is Authorization, injected by the CDK's HTTPSession from TokenSource. Recording it as a defaultHeader would misrepresent it as a constant.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.params.fields (literal: Each model ships an explicit ClassVar `fields` list (dozens of entries per stream, in fields.py/models.py), but the list actually sent is rewritten at request time by PermissionManager and can be further trimmed by the permission-error retry path. Emitting the shipped list as if it were the wire value would be misleading, so only the shape is recorded.
abstained.streams[0].pull.snapshot.recordsPath: AdAccount has endpoint == "", so the request goes to /act_{id}/ and the response is parsed by FacebookSingleResponse (the resource object at the JSON root), not by the paginated {data: [...]} envelope. There is no records path.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.paginator.terminateOn (: For incremental backfill legs the connector issues exactly ONE request per invocation and persists paging.cursors.after into connector state as the page cursor; termination across invocations is driven by the CDK's page-cursor protocol (a null FacebookCursor ends the backfill), not by an in-loop condition. `absent_token` is recorded because that is the condition that yields the terminal null, but the loop itself lives in the CDK.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow (entit: The Graph API's own retention/validity window for a paging cursor is not stated anywhere in the connector, and stale `after` cursors are not handled specially. Only the insights-side windows (37 months, 1h job wait) are code-evidenced.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition (insights): Insights bindings are opened with fetch_page/fetch_changes and a FacebookResource tombstone like the other incremental streams, so "merge" is inferred from the keyed incremental shape rather than from an explicit disposition setting; the CDK, not this connector, decides the materialization semantics.
abstained.discovery: Not applicable: the stream list is a fixed set of Python model classes plus one extra stream per custom_insights config entry. No schema/catalog is read from the customer's account to enumerate streams. (The `_discover_entity_ids` helper in the insights job manager discovers campaign/adset/ad IDs for job splitting, not streams.)
